title: 172. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Multiplying Polynomials
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Multiplying a Monomial by a Binomial
questions.learningObjective: Expand a product of a monomial and a binomial using the distributive property.
questions.question: Expand \(3x(x+4)\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply \(3x\) by each term inside the parentheses:
\[
3x(x+4)=3x\cdot x+3x\cdot 4=3x^2+12x
\]
Therefore, the expanded form is \(3x^2+12x\).
questions.hint: Distribute the monomial to every term inside the parentheses.

questions.concept: Multiplying a Negative Monomial by a Binomial
questions.learningObjective: Expand a product involving a negative monomial and a binomial.
questions.question: Expand \(-2x(3x-5)\).
questions.explanation:
Distribute \(-2x\) to each term:
\[
-2x(3x-5)=(-2x)(3x)+(-2x)(-5)=-6x^2+10x
\]
Therefore, the expanded form is \(-6x^2+10x\).
questions.hint: Remember that multiplying two negative quantities gives a positive result.

questions.concept: Multiplying Two Binomials with Positive Constants
questions.learningObjective: Expand a product of two binomials and combine like terms.
questions.question: Expand \((x+2)(x+5)\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply each term in the first binomial by each term in the second, then combine the like terms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(x+2)(x+5) &= x^2+5x+2x+10\\
&= x^2+7x+10
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the expanded form is \(x^2+7x+10\).
questions.hint: Multiply each term of one binomial by each term of the other, then combine like terms.

questions.concept: Multiplying Binomials with a Negative Constant
questions.learningObjective: Expand a product of two binomials involving subtraction and combine like terms.
questions.question: Expand \((x-3)(x+4)\).
questions.explanation:
Use the distributive property, then combine the like terms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(x-3)(x+4) &= x^2+4x-3x-12\\
&= x^2+x-12
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the expanded form is \(x^2+x-12\).
questions.hint: Pay attention to the sign when multiplying the negative term by each term in the other binomial.

questions.concept: Multiplying Binomials with a Leading Coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Expand a product of two binomials where one has a leading coefficient.
questions.question: Expand \((2x+1)(x-3)\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply each pair of terms, then combine the \(x\) terms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(2x+1)(x-3) &= 2x^2-6x+x-3\\
-6x+x &= -5x
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the expanded form is \(2x^2-5x-3\).
questions.hint: Multiply all four pairs of terms, then combine the two \(x\) terms.

questions.concept: Multiplying Two Binomials with Leading Coefficients
questions.learningObjective: Expand a product of two binomials that both have leading coefficients.
questions.question: Expand \((3x-2)(2x+5)\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply each pair of terms, then combine the \(x\) terms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(3x-2)(2x+5) &= 6x^2+15x-4x-10\\
15x-4x &= 11x
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the expanded form is \(6x^2+11x-10\).
questions.hint: Use the distributive property carefully, then combine the \(x\) terms.

questions.concept: Multiplying a Binomial by a Trinomial
questions.learningObjective: Expand a product of a binomial and a trinomial and combine like terms.
questions.question: Expand \((x+2)(x^2-3x+4)\).
questions.explanation:
Distribute \(x+2\) to each term of the trinomial, then combine like terms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(x+2)(x^2-3x+4) &= x^3-3x^2+4x+2x^2-6x+8\\
&= x^3+(-3x^2+2x^2)+(4x-6x)+8\\
&= x^3-x^2-2x+8
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the expanded form is \(x^3-x^2-2x+8\).
questions.hint: Multiply each term of the binomial by every term of the trinomial, then combine like terms.

questions.concept: Multiplying a Binomial with a Leading Coefficient by a Trinomial
questions.learningObjective: Expand a product of a binomial with a leading coefficient and a trinomial.
questions.question: Expand \((2x-1)(x^2+3x-2)\).
questions.explanation:
Distribute \(2x-1\) to each term of the trinomial, then combine like terms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(2x-1)(x^2+3x-2) &= 2x^3+6x^2-4x-x^2-3x+2\\
&= 2x^3+(6x^2-x^2)+(-4x-3x)+2\\
&= 2x^3+5x^2-7x+2
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the expanded form is \(2x^3+5x^2-7x+2\).
questions.hint: Multiply each term of the binomial by every term of the trinomial, then simplify.

questions.concept: Multiplying Polynomials to Form a Sum of Cubes
questions.learningObjective: Expand a binomial multiplied by a trinomial to recognize a special product.
questions.question: Expand \((x+y)(x^2-xy+y^2)\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply each term; the middle terms cancel:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(x+y)(x^2-xy+y^2) &= x^3-x^2y+xy^2+x^2y-xy^2+y^3\\
&= x^3+y^3
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the expanded form is \(x^3+y^3\).
questions.hint: Look for pairs of like terms that cancel after multiplication.

questions.concept: Multiplying a Binomial by a Trinomial with Two Variables
questions.learningObjective: Expand a product of a binomial and a trinomial containing two variables.
questions.question: Expand \((a+b)(a^2-2ab+b^2)\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply each term, then combine like terms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(a+b)(a^2-2ab+b^2) &= a^3-2a^2b+ab^2+a^2b-2ab^2+b^3\\
&= a^3+(-2a^2b+a^2b)+(ab^2-2ab^2)+b^3\\
&= a^3-a^2b-ab^2+b^3
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the expanded form is \(a^3-a^2b-ab^2+b^3\).
questions.hint: Multiply each term of the binomial by every term of the trinomial, then combine like terms carefully.
